gift-shopping.title: The wishlist that actually travels with you
gift-shopping.lead: Amazon lists, bookmarks, texts to yourself, screenshots — gift ideas scatter the moment you save them. Tote keeps everything in one place, organized by occasion, ready to share.

answer.question: How do you keep a gift wishlist usable across different stores?
answer.answer: Save links from different stores, come back later to compare them, mark the gifts that matter most, and share the shortlist when you're ready. Tote keeps the list usable after the moment you save it.

gift-shopping.intro: You spot a perfect gift in June and save it somewhere — a browser bookmark, a text to yourself, an Amazon list. By December, you can't find it. Meanwhile, your family is asking what you want, and you're texting links back and forth. Someone buys the same thing twice. Nobody has a clear picture of what's been covered.
gift-shopping.solutionHeading: From scattered links to a clear shortlist

cards.title: Save from any store
cards.description: Amazon, Etsy, small boutiques, brand sites — wherever you find the gift, it lands in the same list instead of disappearing into tabs or notes.

cards.title: Keep the shortlist moving
cards.description: Compare options side by side, mark favorites, and use selections when you want to signal “pick one of these” instead of leaving people guessing.

cards.title: Share when it matters
cards.description: Send the list to family or make it public when you're ready. Everyone sees the same shortlist, so duplicate gifts and back-and-forth messages drop off fast.

gift-shopping.setupIntro: A simple gift list usually works best:
setup: Create one collection for the occasion: “Holiday Wishlist {{year}}”, “Birthday Wishlist”, or “Registry Ideas”
Add slots only if they help the decision: “Big gifts”, “Under $50”, or one slot per recipient
Use selections to mark the gifts you actually want family to focus on

steps.lead: Save gift ideas as you browse.
steps.body: Install the Chrome extension, then click to save any product page to a gift collection. Tote captures the name, image, price, and link automatically.
Keep the shortlist in one place, refresh prices if needed, and mark the gifts that matter most.

steps.lead: Share the decision, not the chaos.
steps.body: Send one link to family or friends so they can browse the same list without needing a Tote account.

gift-shopping.tip: Building a holiday list? Set a budget before you start saving. When the shortlist gets longer, you'll still know what is realistic to buy or ask for.

faq.q: Can others see my wishlist?
faq.a: Only if you share it. Collections are private by default. You can share via invite link (recipients need a Tote account) or make the collection public (anyone with the link can view).

faq.q: Can I share with people who don't have Tote?
faq.a: Yes. Public collections can be viewed by anyone — no account required. Just send them the link.

faq.q: How do I avoid duplicate gifts?
faq.a: Share one collection with your family. Everyone can see what's on the list and coordinate who's buying what. Use selections to mark claimed items.

faq.q: Can I use Tote as a gift registry?
faq.a: Tote works well as a lightweight registry. Create a collection, add items from any store, and share the link. It's not a traditional registry with purchase tracking, but it gives everyone a single, up-to-date list to reference.

home-renovation.intro: You're browsing IKEA for a sofa, Wayfair for a rug, a local shop for lighting, and Amazon for hardware. Each store has its own wishlist (or none at all). You're juggling browser tabs, screenshots, and a spreadsheet that's already out of date. Meanwhile, your budget is a moving target and your partner hasn't seen half the options.
home-renovation.solutionHeading: From scattered tabs to room-by-room decisions

cards.title: Save from every store
cards.description: IKEA, Wayfair, Etsy, brand sites, local shops. Everything lands in one place instead of getting split across tabs, screenshots, and a spreadsheet.

cards.title: Keep the project moving room by room
cards.description: Group options by room, compare categories side by side, refresh prices when it matters, and keep the current shortlist visible without rebuilding it every time.

cards.title: Share the same plan
cards.description: Invite your partner to collaborate or send a link to your contractor or designer. Everyone sees the same options, prices, and priorities.

home-renovation.setupIntro: A simple renovation board usually works best:
setup: Create one collection per room: “Living Room”, “Kitchen”, “Primary Bedroom”
Add slots only where they help the decision: “Seating”, “Lighting”, “Rugs”, or “Hardware”
Set a budget before you start comparing products, then use selections to mark the current front-runner

steps.body: Install the browser extension. When you find a piece of furniture or material you like, click to save it to the right room's collection. Tote captures the image, price, and link.
Group items by category (seating, lighting, rugs). Use selections to mark your top picks and compare options side by side.
Add a budget to each collection or slot. Invite your partner to collaborate or share a link with your contractor for review.

home-renovation.tip: When a room gets crowded, trim the list back to a real shortlist. The goal is not to save everything. It is to keep the decision moving.

faq.q: Can I set a budget per room?
faq.a: Each collection (room) can have its own budget. You can also set budgets on individual slots (categories) within a room for even more detail.

faq.q: How do I share with my contractor?
faq.a: Make the collection public and send them the link — they can view everything without creating an account. If you want them to add items too, send an invite link instead.

faq.q: Does it work with IKEA and Wayfair?
faq.a: Tote works with just about any online store — IKEA, Wayfair, Amazon, Etsy, CB2, West Elm, local shops, and more. If you can see a product page, Tote can save it.

faq.q: Can my partner and I both add items?
faq.a: Share the collection via invite link and you can both save products, organize them, and mark selections. Changes show up instantly for both of you.

answer.answer: Save pieces from different stores, come back later to compare them, keep a shortlist of what still fits the plan, and refresh prices when you're ready to buy. Tote keeps your style board usable after the moment you save it.

By the time you're ready to buy, you can't remember what you saved, where you saved it, or whether it's still in stock.
personal-style.solutionHeading: From saved pieces to a wearable shortlist

cards.title: Save from every store
cards.description: Zara, H&M, ASOS, Depop, boutiques. The pieces all land in one board instead of getting lost across bookmarks and store wishlists.

cards.title: Keep the shortlist focused
cards.description: Compare pieces by category, use selections when you want fewer options, and keep the board honest about what still belongs in the wardrobe.

cards.title: Buy when the timing is right
cards.description: Refresh prices to catch sales or sold-out items before you buy. You do not need to revisit every store just to see what changed.

personal-style.setupIntro: A simple wardrobe board usually works best:
setup: Create one collection such as “Capsule Wardrobe”, “Spring Outfits”, or “Vacation Looks”
Add slots only where they help the decision: “Tops”, “Bottoms”, “Shoes”, “Outerwear”
Use selection limits to cap each category and keep the shortlist wearable, not endless

steps.body: Install the Chrome extension. When you see something you like — Zara, H&M, ASOS, Depop, a local boutique — click to save it. Tote captures the image, price, and link.
Sort pieces into collections by season or project. Use slots for categories like tops, bottoms, and shoes. Mark your favorites with selections.
When you're ready to shop, refresh prices to see what's on sale. Click through to buy directly from the original store.

personal-style.tip: Building a capsule wardrobe? Selection limits do more than organize the board. They force the decision.

faq.q: Can I organize by season?
faq.a: Absolutely. Create a collection for each season — “Summer Essentials”, “Winter Basics” — and save relevant pieces into each. You can also use slots within a collection to subdivide by category.

faq.q: How do I track sale prices?
faq.a: Use the price refresh feature to update saved products with their current prices. This lets you spot discounts without visiting each store individually.

faq.q: Does it work with Zara, H&M, and other fashion retailers?
faq.a: It works with just about any online store — Zara, H&M, ASOS, Depop, Nordstrom, Net-a-Porter, boutiques, you name it. If you can see the product page, Tote can save it.

faq.q: Can I share my style board with a friend?
faq.a: Of course. Share via invite link if you want to collaborate, or make it public so anyone with the link can browse your picks.

family-shopping.lead: You text a link. They screenshot a different one. Someone buys the same thing twice. Tote gives your household one shared shopping board, so everyone sees the same options and decisions in one place.

answer.question: How do you keep a shared shopping project usable with another person?
answer.answer: Save links from different stores into one shared board, come back later to compare them together, keep the shortlist moving, and let everyone work from the same plan. Tote replaces text-thread chaos with one place to decide.

family-shopping.setupIntro: A shared project board usually works best when it stays narrow:
setup: Create one collection for a real project such as “New Apartment” or “Back to School”
Add slots only where they help: room-based slots or simple stages like “Comparing” and “Picked”
Invite the other person right away so both people save into the same shortlist from the start

steps.body: One person creates the collection and sends an invite link. The other joins with one click.
Each person browses stores and saves products to the shared collection using the browser extension. Everything appears in one board.
Review the options, mark favorites, set a budget, and buy when you're ready. No more guessing what the other person found.

family-shopping.tip: If a shared board starts feeling noisy, split it by project. One board for “New Apartment” usually works better than one giant board for everything.

faq.q: Can my partner add items too?
faq.a: When you share a collection via invite link, anyone who joins can add products, rearrange items, and mark selections — just like you.

faq.q: Do we both need accounts for a shared shopping list?
faq.a: To add items and collaborate, yes — both people need a free Tote account. But if you just want someone to view your picks, make the collection public and they can browse without an account.

faq.q: Can we have separate collections?
faq.a: Absolutely. Each person has their own private collections by default. You choose which ones to share. Share a “New Home” collection with your partner while keeping your personal “Birthday Wishlist” private.

faq.q: How do we avoid buying the same thing?
faq.a: Everything is in one shared board, so both people can see what's been saved and selected. Use selections to mark which items are “claimed” or decided on.

professional-projects.lead: You're sourcing for three clients, each with their own stores, budget, and taste. The current setup is a spreadsheet, a PDF mood board, and an email chain. Tote keeps every project separate and shareable — no PDF required.

answer.question: How do you keep sourcing decisions usable across client projects?
answer.answer: Save products from different suppliers into one client-facing board, come back later to compare them, keep the shortlist and budget moving, and share the same link for review. Tote keeps sourcing usable after the first round of saves.

cards.description: Trade sites, retail stores, wholesale suppliers, brand sites. Everything lands in one board instead of getting split across spreadsheets and PDFs.

cards.title: Keep the shortlist moving
cards.description: Compare options by room or category, keep the budget visible, and narrow the board to what the client actually needs to review.

cards.title: Share one client-ready board

professional-projects.setupIntro: A clean sourcing workflow usually stays simple:
setup: Create one collection per client or per project phase
Add slots only where they help the review: “Living Room”, “Lighting”, “Tile”, or “Hardware”
Set a budget before you share and use selections to highlight the shortlist you want the client to review

steps.body: Browse supplier websites, retail stores, and trade sites. Save products to the right client collection using the browser extension.
Use slots to group options by room or category. Mark your recommended selections. Set budgets to stay within the client's range.
Send a public link to the client. They see a polished mood board with everything laid out. Update and reshare as many times as you need.

professional-projects.tip: Clients do not need every option you found. They need the shortlist you are ready to stand behind.

faq.q: Can I manage multiple client projects?
faq.a: Absolutely. Create a separate collection for each client or project. They're completely independent — different items, different budgets, different sharing settings.

faq.q: Can clients view without editing?
faq.a: Make the collection public and share the link. Clients can browse the board, see images and prices, and click through to products — but they can't modify anything.

faq.q: How do I share a mood board for approval?
faq.a: Make the collection public, then send the link to your client. They see a visual board with all your curated options. You can update the collection anytime and the link stays the same.

faq.q: Does it work with trade and wholesale sites?
faq.a: Tote works with any website that has product pages — trade sites, retail stores, wholesale suppliers, all of it. If you can view it in a browser, you can save it.
